summary: A real fused cuda::tiles kernel (GlyphScoreV1 + ResidencySortKeyV1 packing in one __tile_global__ kernel) was written and its C++ frontend compiles with ZERO errors against WSL2's genuine CUDA 13.3 cuda_tile.h (4064 lines, real cuda::tiles C++20 API, not a stub). Device-code generation is blocked by a real, confirmed cross-version incompatibility between the only two available cuTile toolchain components in this environment.

backend_source.status: the ONLY tileiras (Tile IR optimizing assembler / backend compiler) binary found anywhere on this WSL2 filesystem -- searched exhaustively. atlas-rapids-cu13's own nvcc has no bundled tileiras despite expecting one.

environment_findings.correction_to_prior_handoff_note: next_steps/active/2026-09-14_gpu-mini-fabric-cutile-level3-and-tests.md and this session's own initial assumption both treated 'WSL2 has cuda_tile.h' as equivalent to 'WSL2 can compile cuTile device code'. This is FALSE -- the header (frontend type system) and the tileiras backend compiler are split across two independently-versioned installations (conda CUDA 13.3 vs pip CUDA 13.2) that were never verified to interoperate before this attempt.

real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.error: calling a __tile__ function from a __host__ function is not allowed
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.cause: tried factoring a shared helper (bid()-wrapping) into a plain function outside tile-kernel context
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.fix: not applicable to final kernel (removed the offending factoring)

real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.error: calling a __tile__ function ... from a __device__ function is not allowed
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.cause: tried factoring popcount SWAR logic into a separate __device__ helper function -- cuda::tiles builtin operators (&, >>, +, -, *) may ONLY be called from directly within a __global__/__tile_global__ tile-kernel body, never from an ordinary __device__ helper
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.fix: inlined the SWAR popcount algorithm via a macro instead of a function

real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.cause: cuda::tiles has no popcount builtin at all (confirmed via grep against the full 4064-line header -- zero matches)
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.fix: implemented standard SWAR bit-count manually using tile arithmetic/bitwise operators, which the header DOES define

real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.error: calling a __tile__ function ... from a __global__ function is not allowed
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.cause: used plain __global__ as the kernel qualifier for a kernel body containing tile operations
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.fix: the correct tile-kernel entry-point qualifier is __tile_global__, NOT __global__ -- confirmed by reading host_defines.h's own macro definitions (__tile_global__ expands to __location__(tile_global), a distinct attribute from __location__(global))

real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.error: accessing gridDim/blockDim/blockIdx/threadIdx/warpSize is unsupported in tile code
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.cause: used blockIdx.x directly inside a __tile_global__ kernel
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.fix: cuda::tiles::bid() (returns uint3) is the tile-code-native equivalent of blockIdx, confirmed against the header's own bid() definition at cuda_tile.h:1783

real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.error: a non-__tile__ variable ("GLYPH_SCORE_W_PAGERANK") cannot be used in tile code
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.cause: LEVEL 2's convention of __device__ __constant__ uint32_t weight constants is illegal to reference from tile code
real_compile_errors_found_and_fixed.fix: changed to plain constexpr uint32_t compile-time literals, which tile code accepts and which still satisfies design.md Decision 1's 'weights are named constants' requirement

backend_blocker_detail.symptom: nvcc's internal tileiras invocation (`tileiras --host-arch=x86_64 --host-os=linux -arch=sm_86 <file>.tilebc -o <file>.tile.cubin`) fails with `error: invalid GPU architecture: 86`, even though sm_86 is confirmed present in tileiras' own embedded architecture string table (verified via `strings tileiras | grep sm_`).
isolation_steps_taken: confirmed tileiras itself works standalone (--version succeeds, exit 0)
confirmed tileiras's LLVM-cl::opt-style arg parser requires the full flag spelling --gpu-name=sm_86, not the abbreviated -arch=sm_86 nvcc passes by default -- fixed this via manual invocation

re-ran tileiras manually with the corrected --gpu-name=sm_86 flag directly against the REAL .tilebc nvcc's cicc (CUDA 13.3) generated for this kernel -- STILL fails with the identical 'invalid GPU architecture: 86' error

conclusion: the failure is not a CLI flag-naming mismatch (which would have been fixed by the --gpu-name= correction) -- it is that CUDA 13.3's cicc embeds the target architecture inside the .tilebc bytecode itself in a format (bare '86') that CUDA 13.2's tileiras cannot parse, independent of what is passed on tileiras' own command line. This is a genuine Tile-IR intermediate-representation version-skew between the 13.3 frontend and 13.2 backend, not a flag or environment-path issue.
backend_blocker_detail.conclusion: the WSL2 atlas-rapids-cu13 (CUDA 13.3) frontend and the only available atlas-cutile-cu132 (CUDA 13.2) backend tileiras are NOT interoperable for this kernel. A matched-version tileiras for CUDA 13.3 (or a matched-version cuda_tile.h + cicc for CUDA 13.2) would be required to complete device-code generation. Neither was located anywhere on this filesystem in this session -- this is a real, not merely inconvenient, blocker.
